title: Cretan stitch
subtitle: A central-spine fill stitch that builds a plaited leaf or band
excerpt: Cretan stitch works from the outer edges of a shape inward to a central spine, alternating stitches left and right to build a plaited fill with a natural central vein.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Cretan stitch entry.
heroPrompt: Cretan stitch filling a leaf shape on linen, the central plaited spine visible, green thread, close-up, natural light.

content.text: Cretan stitch starts at one end of a leaf or band outline and works toward the other end. Each stitch enters from the side edge and exits at the centre, with the thread looping under the needle tip. Left and right stitches alternate, and the crossing threads at the centre build a plaited spine automatically.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton, 2 strands for a fine fill, 3 for a bolder leaf

content.text: Draw a leaf outline and mark a centre vein line. Bring the needle up at the tip of the leaf.
Insert the needle on the left edge, slightly lower. Bring it up on the centre vein line, thread looped under the needle.
Insert on the right edge, same level, bring up on the centre vein. Thread under needle. Pull through.
Continue left-right alternating down to the base of the leaf. The plaited spine forms at the centre.

items.cause: The centre vein guide is not followed consistently.
items.fix: Always bring the needle up directly on the marked centre line.

items.symptom: One side of the leaf fills faster than the other
items.cause: Unequal spacing between left and right stitches.
items.fix: Step down the same amount on each side before the next pair of stitches.

content.text: Cretan stitch fills leaf and petal shapes in crewelwork and folk embroidery. Open Cretan (stitches spaced apart) forms a decorative border. Closed Cretan (stitches touching) fills the shape completely with a flat plaited texture.
